overview: Zapier Natural Language Actions (NLA) uses an API key for authentication. You obtain a key from the Zapier NLA portal and include it in the x-api-key header for all NLA API requests. The NLA API allows you to trigger Zapier actions using natural language descriptions of what to do.

apiKey.label: NLA API Key
apiKey.description: Generated at https://nla.zapier.com/credentials/ after signing into your Zapier account.

steps.title: Sign in to Zapier
steps.description: Go to https://nla.zapier.com and sign in with your Zapier account.
steps.tip: The NLA API is a separate product from Zapier's standard automation builder. Ensure your plan includes NLA API access.

steps.title: Enable actions in the NLA portal
steps.description: In the Zapier NLA portal, browse the available actions (e.g., Gmail: Send Email, Slack: Send Message) and enable the ones your integration needs.
steps.tip: Actions are linked to your existing Zapier connected accounts. Make sure the relevant Zapier integrations are already set up in your Zapier account.

steps.title: Get your NLA API key
steps.description: Go to https://nla.zapier.com/credentials/ to find or generate your NLA API key.
steps.warning: Store the API key securely. It grants access to all enabled NLA actions on your Zapier account.

steps.title: Add the key to Nolixan
steps.description: In Nolixan, create a connection for Zapier NLA with the API key.

tips: The NLA API base URL is https://nla.zapier.com/api/v1/. Use GET /exposed/ to list all enabled actions for a user.
NLA actions are invoked with a plain English description — Zapier maps the description to the correct action and fills in parameters.
For standard Zapier automation (Zaps), the NLA API is not needed. NLA is specifically for programmatic, AI-driven action execution.
warnings: NLA actions execute real tasks (sending emails, posting to Slack, etc.). Test with low-impact actions before enabling high-consequence ones.
The Zapier NLA API is in limited availability. Check https://nla.zapier.com for current access status and API limits.
